metadata.title: The Critical Path
metadata.creator: Sanjana Rao
metadata.note: ai-explainer CONCEPT explainer (AI + Critical Path Method) for @HumanitariansAI, first-person Sanjana Rao (af_bella). Framework = MAP / FIND / PROTECT. Example network A-B-D-E=14 (critical) vs A-C-D-E=11 (C has 3 days slack); non-critical speed-up changes nothing; slack overrun shifts the path.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW -- ClaudeComposerAsk, ask answered; first-person Sanjana
beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sanjana, a project manager at Humanitarians AI. Every project has a deadline, and when it's slipping, the instinct is to speed everything up. But here's the thing most schedules get wrong: only some of your tasks actually control the finish date. The rest have slack. The chain that sets your deadline is called the critical path -- and AI can find it for you in seconds. The trick is knowing what that actually means.

props.command: AI can compute my project's critical path from the task list. What is it actually telling me -- and what should I do with it?
output: the longest chain of dependent tasks sets the deadline
tasks on it have zero slack -- a day late = a day late
speeding up the wrong task changes nothing

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW -- hesitant-writer BLUF; corrects the reel's real misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the whole idea in one breath. It feels like to finish sooner, you speed up any task. You don't. Only the longest chain of dependent tasks -- the critical path -- sets the deadline. Speed up a task that isn't on it, and you've saved nothing. Find that path, and you know exactly where effort actually counts.

Every task moves the deadline.

beats.role_note: SHOW-DON'T-TELL: a task network; the longest chain sets the end date, not every task
beats.narration_text: So picture a small project as a network. Design, then two things can happen at once -- build the backend, build the interface -- then integrate them, then test. The tasks aren't a straight line; some run in parallel. And that's the catch. The backend takes five days, the interface takes two. They both start after design and both feed integration -- so the interface finishing early buys you nothing, because you're still waiting on the backend. The finish date is set by the longest path through the network, not by any single task.

shot.visual_intent: An activity-on-node network: A Design(3) -> B Backend(5) and C UI(2) in parallel -> D Integrate(4) -> E Test(2). Nodes with durations, arrows for dependencies. Show the two branches B(5) vs C(2) converging at D; highlight that D waits for the SLOWER branch. Reframe: the longest path sets the finish, not any one task. Terracotta on the longest branch.

beats.role_note: framework-first (PROOF): MAP / FIND / PROTECT, shown BEFORE any example
beats.narration_text: So to use the critical path well, three steps. One: map. Give the AI the real tasks, their durations, and -- this is the part people skip -- the real dependencies, what must finish before what. The path is only as true as the dependencies you feed it. Two: find. Let the AI compute the critical path -- the longest chain -- and the slack on every other task. Three: protect. Guard the critical path, spend your attention there, and re-check after any change, because the critical path can move. Map, find, protect.

shot.visual_intent: Three steps stacked: 1 MAP (real tasks + durations + DEPENDENCIES) 2 FIND (AI computes the longest chain + slack on the rest) 3 PROTECT (guard the critical path; re-check -- it can move). Each with a one-line meaning. Footer: the path is only as true as the dependencies you feed it. Terracotta on the footer.

beats.role_note: ASK->RESULT LAW -- composer ask that computes the T05 critical path
beats.narration_text: Let's do a real one. Here's that five-task project. Watch me ask the AI to find the critical path and tell me the slack on every task -- not just the answer, the paths it compared to get there.

props.command: Here are my tasks, durations, and dependencies. Find the critical path, show me every path you compared and its length, and give the slack (float) on each task. Don't just give the answer -- show the paths.

beats.role_note: worked example walked through the framework -- compute both paths, slack on the rest
beats.narration_text: And there it is. Two paths run from start to finish. Design, backend, integrate, test is fourteen days. Design, interface, integrate, test is only eleven. The longer one wins -- fourteen days is the critical path, and every task on it has zero slack: a day late there is a day late for the whole project. The interface branch? It has three days of slack. It can slip three full days and the deadline never moves. That's not a problem to fix -- that's a buffer you can use.

shot.visual_intent: The network with both paths traced: A-B-D-E = 14 (highlighted terracotta = CRITICAL, zero slack) and A-C-D-E = 11. A slack bar on C shows '3 days slack'. Numbers add up on screen (3+5+4+2=14, 3+2+4+2=11). Verdict: critical path = 14 days. Terracotta on the critical chain; muted on the slack branch.

beats.role_note: falsifiability -- speeding up a non-critical task does nothing; slack overrun shifts the path
beats.narration_text: Now the mistake almost everyone makes. The deadline's tight, so someone says: crash the interface, get it done in one day instead of two. Feels productive. But watch the finish date -- it doesn't move. Still fourteen days, because the interface was never on the critical path. You spent effort and saved nothing. And here's the twist that catches people: if that interface branch slips the other way -- say it blows past its three days of slack and takes six -- now its path is fifteen days, longer than the backend's. The critical path just moved. So you don't find it once. You watch it.

shot.visual_intent: Two moves on the network. MOVE 1: shrink C 2->1; the finish stays 14 (a red 'no change' on the deadline) -- speeding a non-critical task does nothing. MOVE 2: grow C past its slack (to 6); the A-C-D-E path becomes 15 > 14 and the critical path SHIFTS to the C branch (terracotta jumps to A-C-D-E). Caption: the critical path moves -- watch it. Terracotta/red on the shift.

beats.role_note: reusable rubric restated -- AI FINDS the path; you PROTECT it and re-check
beats.narration_text: So here's the rule for any schedule. Let the AI find the critical path -- it compares every route faster than you can by hand. But you protect it: put your best people and your attention on that chain, treat slack elsewhere as a buffer, and re-check the path every time something changes. The AI finds the longest path. You keep it from getting longer.

shot.visual_intent: A clean router: LEFT 'AI FINDS -- the longest path, fast'. A center gate = MAP / FIND / PROTECT. RIGHT 'YOU PROTECT -- guard it, re-check'. High negative space, terracotta accent on the gate.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW -- ClaudeComposerAsk 'Your turn.'; prompt read aloud + discussed
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take your own project's tasks and run this. Give the AI your tasks, durations, and dependencies, and ask for three things: the critical path, the slack on every other task, and -- this is the useful part -- what the new critical path would be if your riskiest task slipped by a week. That last answer tells you which 'safe' task is one bad week away from becoming your problem. A good answer shows its paths. A bad one gives a single number with no reasoning -- and a critical path with no paths behind it is just a guess.

props.segment: Run it on your own schedule

Show your reasoning, not just the answer.
